title: Upper deviation probabilities for the range of a supercritical super-Brownian motion
abstract: Let $\{X_t\}_{t\geq 0 }$ be a $d$-dimensional supercritical super-Brownian motion started from the origin with branching mechanism $ψ$. Denote by $R_t:=\inf\{r>0:X_s(\{x\in \mathbb{R}^d:|x|\geq r\})=0,~\forall~0\leq s\leq t\}$ the radius of the minimal ball (centered at the origin) containing the range of $\{X_s\}_{s\geq 0 }$ up to time $t$. In \cite{Pinsky}, Pinsky proved that condition on non-extinction, $\lim_{t\to\infty}R_t/t=\sqrt{2β}$ in probability, where $β:=-ψ'(0)$. Afterwards, Engländer \cite{Englander04} studied the lower deviation probabilities of $R_t$. For the upper deviation probabilities, he \cite[Conjecture 8]{Englander04} conjectured that for $ρ>\sqrt {2β}$, $$ \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{1}{t}\log\mathbb{P}(R_t\geq ρt)=-\left(\frac{ρ^2}{2}-β\right). $$ In this note, we confirmed this conjecture.
